Google Is Stealing Your International Search Traffic :warning: 

It’s happening right now, and it might be worse than you think :arrow_down:

(Big thanks to Erik Sarissky and the team at Ahrefs for surfacing this. Article link in the comments)

Since March 2025, Google has started auto-translating English pages and hosting them on <http://translate.google.com|translate.google.com>.

Your content.
Now showing up without you.

In many countries like India, Brazil, Indonesia, or Türkiye, chances are Google is already serving translated versions of your site.

But here’s the kicker:

Those users?
They never land on your website.

And that traffic?
Now appears as <http://translate.google.com|translate.google.com> / referral
(breaking your analytics at the same time!)

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴?

Because 49% of websites are still in English only.

But Google is looking for quality content to reference in many other languages

To close the gap, Google leaned on auto-translations.

These auto-translated versions can appear everywhere on Google:
• AI Overviews
• Featured snippets
• Even classic blue links

𝗦𝗼 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀?
→ Translate your site
→ Add hreflang tags
→ Give Google your version of the content, not theirs

Even a basic translation of key pages can knock Google’s proxies out of the results (and display your translated version instead)

Weglot can help, of course:
→ Display your site in multiple languages in minutes (taking care of all the technical setup, including hreflang tags)
→ Combine AI + human-reviewed translations
→ Host your content — not Google

Take back your international audience.
Before Google owns it.
